# Quarto Website Reminder

The official documentation for Quarto Websites is:

<https://quarto.org/docs/websites/>

Creating a basic Quarto website is super easy by following these steps in Positron:

1) Click on the __New__ tab in the top left corner

2) Select __New File__

3) Choose __Quarto Project__ > __Website Project__

4) Select a location/directory for your project, and give it a name (e.g. `website`)

5) Click __Create__

And in RStudio:

1) Click on the __File__ tab in the menu bar

2) Select __New Project ...__ 

3) Choose __Quarto Website__

4) Select a location/directory for your project, and give it a name (e.g. `website`)

5) Click __Create__


## Your Turn: Create a Quarto Website

Follow the steps listed above to create a Quarto Website for this workshop.


## File Structure

Positron will open a new session containing your Quarto website with the 
following file structure:

```
website/
  .quarto/
  _quarto.yml
  index.qmd
  about.qmd
  styles.css
```



in RStudio:

```
website/
  .quarto/
  _quarto.yml
  index.qmd
  about.qmd
  styles.css
```

In Positron, the `.quarto` and in RStudio, the `.Rproj` extensions are auxiliary files used by RStudio to recognize that the contents of this directory constitute a project. 

The yaml file `_quarto.yml` is the configuration file.

The quarto files `index.qmd` and `about.qmd` are the default files that get
rendered into the pages of the actual website.

The `styles.css` file is a _cascading style-sheet_ file to optionally customize the
appearance and format of your website.

These files create a very basic website template, which we can preview and then makes edits to for personalization. 


## Previewing your website

One option to preview your website is with the `quarto preview` command. 
In Positron/RStudio, go to the quadrant or pane that has the tab __Terminal__. This is  the same quadrant where the R console is located.

In the terminal, type the following command:

```{.markdown filename="Terminal"}
quarto preview
```

\

### Your Turn: Edit `_quarto.yml` file

In order to get a similar website to our sample demo, you'll begin by editing
your file `_quarto.yml` so that it has the content shown below. Customize the 
`title` option to your _First_ and _Last_ names or your preferred name.

If you get a message indicating that you don't have a `resume.qmd` file, then
simply create one and add it to your website.

```{.markdown filename="_quarto.yml"}
project:
  type: website

website:
  title: "Your Name"
  navbar:
    background: primary
    right:
      - href: index.qmd
        text: Home
      - href: about.qmd
        text: About
      - resume.qmd

format:
  html:
    theme: yeti
    css: styles.css
    toc: true
```

\

### Your Turn: Customizing the Home Page

The next file you'll edit is the `index.qmd` file located at the top level,
which is basically your Home page. Here are some ideas for your `index.qmd` file:

- Include a headshot.
- Include a welcoming paragraph.
- Include links to your linkedin account, github account, twitter, etc.

<a href="https://github.com/gastonstat/quarto-website-ketzaly1/blob/main/index.qmd" target="_blank">https://github.com/gastonstat/quarto-website-ketzaly1/blob/main/index.qmd</a>

In our sample website, `index.qmd` has the following content. Note the use of 
the `about` option which in turn contains further options such as `template`, 
`image`, and `links`.

```{.markdown filename="index.qmd"}
---
title: "Welcome"
about:
  template: jolla
  image: assets/headshot.png
  links:
    - icon: linkedin
      text: LinkedIn
      href: https://www.linkedin.com
      target: _blank # opens link in a new browser tab
    - icon: github
      text: Github
      href: https://github.com
      target: _blank # opens link in a new browser tab
    - icon: twitter
      text: twitter
      href: https://twitter.com
      target: _blank # opens link in a new browser tab
---

Hi there! I'm Ket Zaly, and I'm a Jedi padawan at the Force Academy. 
I love podracing, learning about Kyber crystals, and reading old Jedi
manuscripts. One more thing, I hate the Galactic Empire.
```

Notice that the yaml section in the example `index.qmd` uses the `about:` 
option which in turn includes a _template_ option: `template: jolla`.

There is also an `image` option linking to the headshot file. The associated
file `headshot.png` is stored in the `assets/` folder.

Likewise, there is an option `links` to LinkedIn, Github, and twitter.

```{.markdown filename="Terminal"}
quarto preview
```

### Your Turn: Customizing the About Page

The following file you'll edit is the `about.qmd` file. 

You can tell the world a little bit about you, for instance:

- What your major (or minor) is
- What year you are in
- Are you a member of one or more clubs or student associations?
- Hobbies, interests, fun facts
- Favorite quote(s)
- ETC

<a href="https://github.com/gastonstat/quarto-website-ketzaly1/blob/main/about.qmd" target="_blank">https://github.com/gastonstat/quarto-website-ketzaly1/blob/main/about.qmd</a>

In our sample website, `about.qmd` has the following content.

```{.markdown filename="about.qmd"}
---
title: "A little bit about me"
---

I am originally from South Corellia.

I am double majoring in Jedi Studies and Lightsabers Engineering at the Force Academy.

On my spare free time I like to read old Jedi manuscripts especially the sacred Jedi texts dating back to the dawn of the Jedi Order. I also enjoy science fiction books by Wookie authors, and I love to watch documentaries about the moon of Endor. Likewise, I like to bake & bike.

One of my favorite quotes is:

> "Do or do not. There is no try".
>
> Jedi Grand Master Yoda


My all time favorite poem is _This is the Way_ by Din Djarin.

Have I mentioned that I love PB&J?

My favorite colors are `#FF0000` and `#FFFFFF`.

I own an R3-series personal droid that my grandparents gave me on my 7th birthday.

Last but not least ...
```

To preview your website, run the following command:

```{.markdown filename="Terminal"}
quarto preview
```

::: {.callout-warning}
Because your website will be publicly available, we recommend to include only
information that you feel comfortable sharing with the world. Put another way,
don't share things that you would be embarrassed of, or that you don't want
future employers to find about you. Keep it professional.
:::

\

# Previewing, Rendering, and Publishing

As we mentioned before, one way to preview your website is by running the 
`quarto preview` command in Terminal:

```{.markdown filename="Terminal"}
quarto preview
```


## Rendering your website to `_site/`

To render (but not preview) a website, use the `quarto render` command, which 
will render the website into the `_site` directory by default.
In the terminal, type the following command:

```{.markdown filename="Terminal"}
quarto render
```

Once the website gets rendered to the `_site` directory, you can click on any 
of the HTML files in this directory---e.g. `index.html`---to visualize your
website in your browser. Do this sporadically after making changes to ensure you like the edits you have made.
 

-----


# Adding a Projects Tab to Your Website

The next addition to the website involves adding a `Projects` tab with its
corresponding webpage, and also embedding your dashboard from Pub 7. 

## Your Turn: Add projects content

1) Create a folder `projects`.

2) Inside `projects`, create an `index.qmd` file. This will become the 
page of the __Projects__ tab.

3) Also inside `projects`, create a folder `dashboard`. This will contain another quarto file with your dashboard from Pub 7. 

Your file structure should look like this:

```
website/
  .quarto/
  _quarto.yml
  assets/
    headshot.png
  index.qmd
  about.qmd
  resume.qmd
  projects/
    index.qmd
    dashboard/
      ...
  styles.css
```

Browse the content of `projects` in our sample website, and feel free to 
copy-paste a quarto documents contained in this folder and its
subdirectories if you would like to add more content.

<a href="https://github.com/gastonstat/quarto-website-ketzaly1/tree/main/projects" target="_blank">https://github.com/gastonstat/quarto-website-ketzaly1/tree/main/projects</a>


After you've saved the changes in all files, preview your website. If you are happy with your website, continue to publishing.


### Publishing website to Netlify

To publish your website to Netlify by dragging your website folder to the 'Add new project' > 'Upload your project files' section. Don't forget to rename your website link! Refer to today's lab slides for more in-depth instructions.
